title: The plan skill asks what it does not know before it proposes
description:
`plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md` goes from step 2 (read the repository) straight to step 3 (decompose into nodes) with nothing in between that returns to the user, so an ambiguous request becomes nodes with no scope check and the misreading is only found after the board has been written.

Add one step between the current 2 and 3: where two readings of the request would produce different nodes, put the question to the user and wait for the answer before decomposing; where the request is already specific, do not invent a question to have one. Say what this is not — it is not one of the four decision categories, and a question about state, module boundaries, data flow or error handling still goes on the board through `propose` rather than being asked here. Keep it short: this file is prose four hosts read, and the part that drifts first is the part nobody re-reads.

Then run `pnpm plugins` and commit the generated files. `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` fails if they are not current.

brief.approach:
One paragraph in one file, then the generator. Score 2: prose only, but prose four hosts read, and the generated copies have to land in the same commit.

**Where.** `plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md`. The numbered list runs 1 (read the board) -> 2 (read the repository) -> 3 (decompose into nodes), and there is nothing between 2 and 3 that returns to the user. Insert a new step **3**, renumbering the current 3-7 to 4-8. Check with `rg -n 'step [0-9]' plugins/ docs/` that no other skill or document cites this file's step numbers before you shift them; the closing line after the last step stands alone and needs no change.

**What the step says**, in this file's own register — imperative, short sentences, bold for the rule and not for emphasis:

- Where two readings of the request would produce different nodes, put that question to the user and wait. Name the two readings; do not ask an open "what did you mean".
- Where the request is already specific, ask nothing. A question invented to have one costs the user a turn and teaches them to skim the next one.
- Say what this is **not**: it is not one of the four decision categories. A question about state, module boundaries, data flow or error handling is a decision, and it goes on the board through `propose` in what becomes step 5 — it is not asked here. This is the one distinction that will be got wrong, so it needs its own sentence.
- Ask with this host's own question tool, the way the rest of the plugin asks (ADR 0057), not by writing a question into a node's description.

Keep it to roughly the length of step 2. This file is read by an agent on four hosts and the part that drifts first is the part nobody re-reads; a step longer than the one before it is the part that gets skimmed.

**Then the generator.** `pnpm plugins` (`scripts/build-plugins.mjs`) writes the four copies — `packages/claude-code-plugin/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `packages/codex-plugin/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `packages/cursor-plugin/skills/plan/SKILL.md`, `packages/opencode-plugin/.opencode/skills/plan/SKILL.md`. Commit them with the source in one commit; `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` is the drift check and fails while they disagree. Never hand-edit a generated copy.

Nothing else changes: no tool, no schema, no core. The node that makes a new node check itself against the board (`a-new-node-is-checked-against-the-nodes-0ny5`) waits on this one and owns that step — do not write it here.

acceptance.proves: the four generated plan skills match plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md after pnpm plugins — the new step reaches every host rather than only the source
a step was inserted and the list renumbered through to the end, rather than a paragraph dropped in with two steps sharing a number

acceptance.run: grep -qi 'not one of the four' plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md
acceptance.proves: the new step says explicitly that this is not a decision category — the one distinction an agent will otherwise collapse, turning every ambiguity into a board decision
only the plan skill and its four generated copies changed: no tool, no schema, no core, and no other skill was touched
